t.1.205.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus made the agreement, the Pāṇḍavas dwelt there, bringing other kings under their control by the might of their weapons.
t.1.205.2: Kṛṣṇā became obedient to all of them, those five lions among men, the Pārthas of boundless might.
t.1.205.4: While the great-souled Pāṇḍavas conducted themselves according to dharma, all the Kurus prospered, free from faults and endowed with happiness.
t.1.205.3: They were supremely delighted with her, and she too, together with those five heroic husbands, was supremely delighted, like the Sarasvatī with the Nāgas.
t.1.205.5: Then, after a long time, O lord of the people, some thieves carried off the cows of a certain brāhmaṇa, O best of kings.
t.1.205.6: As that wealth was being carried off, the brāhmaṇa, overwhelmed with anger, came to Khāṇḍavaprastha and cried out loudly to the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.205.8: The oblation of a heedless brahmin is plundered by crows; a base jackal violates the empty cave of the tiger.
t.1.205.9: A Brahmin's property has been stolen by thieves, the purpose of dharma is being destroyed, and I am crying out loudly; let weapons be taken up!
t.1.205.7: Cattle-wealth is being carried off by force from this realm of yours by base, cruel men of unrestrained spirit! Rush to the rescue, O Pāṇḍavas!
t.1.205.10: Near that brahmin, who was crying out loudly again and again, the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya, son of Kuntī, heard those words.
t.1.205.11: Having heard this, the mighty-armed one said to that brahmin, "Do not be afraid." But where the weapons of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas were kept, there Yudhiṣṭhira, the King of Dharma, was sitting with Kṛṣṇā.
t.1.205.12: The Pāṇḍava was able neither to go in nor to go away; urged again and again by those words of the distressed man, the son of Kuntī, grieved by that cry for help, pondered there.
t.1.205.13: As that wealth of the poor brāhmaṇa was being carried off, he became resolved: "I must wipe away his tears."
t.1.205.14: A very great unrighteousness, born of neglect, would fall upon the king, if today I do not give protection to this man who weeps at the gate.
t.1.205.15: And faithlessness regarding the protection given by all of us would become established in this world, and unrighteousness would surely be ours.
t.1.205.17: If I enter upon the king, exile in the forest will be my lot; yet let there be great adharma, or let my death come in the forest, for dharma prevails even at the cost of the body's destruction.
t.1.205.16: And if I were to go without taking leave of the king, there is no doubt that it would be displeasing to King Ajātaśatru, and to me as well.
t.1.205.18: Having thus resolved, O lord of the people, Kuntī's son Dhanaṃjaya then went in to the king and took his leave of him.
t.1.205.20: Those vile wretches have not gone far; let us go together at once, so that today I may bring back your wealth from the hands of the thieves.
t.1.205.19: Taking up the bow, he joyfully replied to the brahmin: “Brahmin, come quickly, while those who covet the wealth of others are still within reach!”
t.1.205.21: The mighty-armed one, bearing his bow, clad in armor, mounted on his chariot and flying his banner, pursued the thieves, and having struck them down with his arrows, he won back that wealth.
t.1.205.23: He saluted all his elders and was greeted warmly by them in return, and then he said this to the Dharmarāja: "Let a vow be enjoined upon me."
t.1.205.22: Having brought back to the brahmin what was his and having drunk deep of glory, the Pāṇḍava, the hero Savyasācin, scorcher of foes, returned to the city.
t.1.205.24: The agreement has been transgressed by me through my seeing you; I shall go to dwell in the forest, for this was the agreement made by us.
t.1.205.25: Suddenly addressed with these unwelcome words, the Dharma king Yudhiṣṭhira, stricken with grief, said "How so?" in a faltering voice, a brother to his steadfast brother Guḍākeśa.
t.1.205.26: If I am an authority for you, hear my word, sinless one: whatever displeasing thing you did to me by entering, hero, I forgive it all, and there is no resentment in my heart.
t.1.205.27: For the intrusion of an elder is no injury to the younger, but the intrusion of the younger upon the eldest breaks the rule.
t.1.205.28: Turn back, mighty-armed one, do as I say. For there is no breach of dharma on your part, nor has any offense been done to me.
t.1.205.30: Having taken leave of the king, he, consecrated to a vow of celibacy, went forth to dwell in the forest for twelve years.
t.1.205.29: "One should not practise dharma by pretext": this I have heard from you, sir. I will not swerve from the truth; by the truth I take up my weapon.
